fundamental.headline: Solid business, but expensive
fundamental.health: Sales up 31% over the last year, it keeps 18 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, it carries meaningful debt.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying more than usual: its price vs sales is higher than 79% of the last 5 years. Compared with similar companies, adjusted for growth, it's priced about in line.
drivers: Sales growth is speeding up compared with six months ago.
Profit margins are widening: it keeps more of each sale than a year ago.
news: Recent deal/M&A news is news with no clear direction for the company; the stock hasn't reacted much yet, and it could matter for months.
fundamental.take: Good business, but expensive right now: patience may pay; wait for a better price. This is research, not personal advice.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 24% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 31% last year; 19%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 6% (3 years ago -1%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $6 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 14% (3 years ago -2%). (Tax rate estimated at 21%: effective rate not reported.)

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $64M, up 100% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 53% vs quarterly sales up 37% (days to collect 66 → 74). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.
Profit leans on non-operating gains: net income $2.6B vs operating income $1.6B over the last 12 months (e.g. investment gains or one-offs that may not repeat).

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 19%/yr over 3 years and 22%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 17% vs a 5-year range of -18–17% (median -4%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $2.1B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($1.9B buybacks + $209M dividends) = 1.7% of the company's market value. Share count up 5.8% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $7.35, up 18% in 90 days (up 9% in the last 30); 27 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $4.22, up 4% in 90 days; 7 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By product, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Data center 79% of sales, up 46%; Communications and other 21% of sales, up 10%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +40% vs a year ago · $2.87 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 40%, in step with sales (37%): growth comes from more business, not cost cuts.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 4 quarters running by about 1%: beating is now expected, so a small beat may not lift the stock.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 37% from a year ago and speeding up (from 22% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $17 of operating profit, up from $1 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Only 66% of reported profit became spare cash, usually because of heavy investment; worth watching.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 47× last year's profit; only 19× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Dec 1; analysts expect EPS of $1.10, up 45% from a year ago. It usually moves about 13% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 18% in 90 days (27 raised, 1 cut lately): forecasts are moving up fast.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
